data.title: We Like WDB coco's (TSE:7079) Earnings For More Than Just Statutory Profit
data.description:
WDB coco Co., Ltd.'s (TSE:7079) solid earnings announcement recently didn't do much to the stock price. We did some digging, and we think that investors are missing some encouraging factors in the underlying numbers.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

A Closer Look At WDB coco's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, WDB coco had an accrual ratio of -0.26. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of JP¥938m, well over the JP¥732.0m it reported in profit. WDB coco shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

Our Take On WDB coco's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, WDB coco's accrual ratio indicates strong conversion of profit to free cash flow, which is a positive for the company. Because of this, we think WDB coco's underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! Cube System shareholders will no doubt be hoping that its free cash flow bounces back next year, since it was down over the last twelve months. However, that's not all there is to consider. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part.

Check out our latest analysis for Cube System

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Cube System.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that Cube System's profit was boosted by unusual items worth JP¥377m in the last twelve months. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. When we crunched the numbers on thousands of publicly listed companies, we found that a boost from unusual items in a given year is often not repeated the next year. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

Our Take On Cube System's Profit Performance

Summing up, Cube System received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. For the reasons mentioned above, we think that a perfunctory glance at Cube System's statutory profits might make it look better than it really is on an underlying level. data.title: Surprised By AMG Critical Materials' Slide? What Investors Overlooked
data.description:
If an investor bought AMG Critical Materials at the start of 2026 expecting a green metals tailwind and firm backing from US and EU policymakers, the outcome so far has been uncomfortable. For AMG Critical Materials shareholders, the loss from the start of the year was 20.3%, including dividends. With chrome capacity opening in Pennsylvania and EU lithium projects gaining Strategic Project status partway through the period, the question is which of the original assumptions on 7.3% revenue growth, 8.4% margins and an 8.6x future P/E did not fully account for how the story would actually unfold?

AMG Critical Materials has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 33 best rare earth metal stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On AMG Critical Materials

The shares cost €28.4 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at AMG Critical Materials then had to choose between two very different stories about what came next.

On the bullish side, one camp saw a green metals build out in the US and EU and attached a Fair Value of €32.06. This was a price those assumptions pointed to rather than a quoted fact, built on 7.3% revenue growth and an 8.4% profit margin.

The more cautious view put more weight on lithium volatility and geopolitics, using a Fair Value of €20.22 based on revenue declining 0.8% a year and a 6.6x future P/E assumption, despite margins reaching 8.3%.

What The Results Changed For AMG Critical Materials

The strongest evidence came from AMG Critical Materials reporting Q3 2026 revenue of US$471.5m and net income of US$22.8m, with net margin rising to 4.8%. That moved profitability in the right direction for the bullish margin story, although the outcome stayed well below the 8.4% margin the optimistic case had in mind. Overall, the period cut both ways.

The lesson here is clear. When a thesis relies on margin expansion, focus on the reported net margin each quarter and compare it directly with the margin embedded in your original story.

What You Are Paying For In AMG Critical Materials Today

AMG Critical Materials now trades at €23.28, after a share price that fell 20.3% from the start of the year. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St sets its Fair Value above that level, based on an integrated lithium and recycling build out story rather than broad commodity exposure.

The distinctive hook is project execution, from the Bitterfeld lithium refinery through Zinnwald and the Saudi vanadium supercenter. For that higher Fair Value to be reached, a buyer today would need confidence that the lithium and recycling pipeline ramps broadly in line with current expectations.

"The main thing that has to go right is successful execution of the lithium and recycling growth pipeline, including ramp up of the Bitterfeld refinery, integration of Zinnwald and the Saudi vanadium project, while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and balance sheet strength."

One Narrative disagrees with today's price. → See where this Narrative says AMG Critical Materials should trade

Looking One Step Beyond AMG

AMG Critical Materials directs attention to lithium, chrome and recycling. Yet your broader metals exposure does not have to stop there.

Green build outs still need something more old fashioned. They need a way to turn persistent inflation and currency worries into a store of value.

Another miner focuses on supplying gold along with copper and a few other metals. It leans on long life deposits and aims to reset its cost base.

Those moves are meant to keep operations resilient if input costs stay stubborn. If that happens, its place in portfolios could diverge sharply from AMG Critical Materials.

data.title: We Think That There Are Issues Underlying KORCHIP's (KOSDAQ:126730) Earnings
data.description:
Last week's profit announcement from KORCHIP Inc. (KOSDAQ:126730) was underwhelming for investors, despite headline numbers being robust. Our analysis uncovered some concerning factors that we believe the market might be paying attention to.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

A Closer Look At KORCHIP's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, KORCHIP recorded an accrual ratio of -0.10. Therefore, its statutory earnings were quite a lot less than its free cashflow. To wit, it produced free cash flow of ₩11b during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of ₩7.78b. KORCHIP did see its free cash flow drop year on year, which is less than ideal, like a Simpson's episode without Groundskeeper Willie. Having said that, there is more to the story. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

See our latest analysis for KORCHIP

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of KORCHIP.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

While the accrual ratio might bode well, we also note that KORCHIP's profit was boosted by unusual items worth ₩1.9b in the last twelve months. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. When we analysed the vast majority of listed companies worldwide, we found that significant unusual items are often not repeated. Which is hardly surprising, given the name. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

Our Take On KORCHIP's Profit Performance

In conclusion, KORCHIP's accrual ratio suggests its statutory earnings are of good quality, but on the other hand the profits were boosted by unusual items. Having considered these factors, we don't think KORCHIP's statutory profits give an overly harsh view of the business. So while earnings quality is important, it's equally important to consider the risks facing KORCHIP at this point in time.
